title: Seat a clip-on wheel balance weight on the marked rim
instruction: Hang the clip-on balance weight at the green marks on the rim and seat its spring clip with the wheel-weight hammer. Put the hammer back and leave both hands clear for the pull test.
setup: On a rigid bench fixture, two green marks identify the target on a stationary rim flange. A 29 g weight with two sprung jaws starts on the left rest and a 120 g hammer starts on the right. Reset both implements on their open rests and start both grippers clear.
scoring: 0.25 for picking up the weight with the left gripper off the mark and hooking it at the mark with measured rim contact. 0.50 cumulative after a right-hand-held hammer nose contacts the bridge with more than 0.002 N s of impulse from contacts whose recent vertical closing speed exceeds 0.12 m/s. 1.00 after both toes have seated under the lip and the released clip stays at the mark with rim contact and at most 1 mm drift across 60 consecutive full-load frames at 4 N, both hands clear and the released hammer resting steadily on both rack supports throughout. The drift reference is the first eligible full-load position.
context: Installing a counterweight at a pre-marked position isolates the manual fastening step of wheel balancing.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, two sprung hinges and native contacts approximate the clip and flange. A virtual tester ramps an upward force at the crown. The 4 N load and fixture dimensions are benchmark parameters. Hardware retention and dynamic wheel balance have not been measured.
reset_notes: Start one fresh episode with seed 0. The rim, marks and tool rests are fixed. Restore the USD initial poses, neutral spring state and initial arm posture.
scores: Scripted YAM seed 0 scored 1.00 in 479 steps (23.95 s). Dream-1 seed 0 scored 0.00 in 490 steps (24.50 s), stop reason step_limit.
